vedic_reference.root_origin: Sanskrit word for existence or universe
vedic_reference.note: Prathamik strētsuk is a Sanskrit term that signifies the primary or fundamental existence or universe. It is a combination of two roots - pratham (first, primary) and īk (existence, universe). This term is not directly mentioned in the Vedas but is an essential concept in Indian philosophy and spirituality.

historical_references.reference: Prathvik is a Sanskrit name that was believed to be used in ancient India for a divine being who personified the radiance and brilliance of the sun. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'pratha' (foremost) and 'vik' (brilliance).

Prathvik is also a name used in medieval India for a warrior king who ruled over the northern regions of the Deccan Plateau. His reign is believed to have taken place around the 14th century CE during the Bahamani Sultanate period.
